overrides.reason: «ضع خطةً عائليةً متّفقًا عليها» is correct Arabic: متّفقًا is a نعت سببي describing خطة through «عليها», so it takes the masculine accusative. Nothing to fix.

The Arabic is coherent as written (all people err; bad habits are to be reproached). The proposed «لا يعيبه على الخطأ بل…» is a speculative reconstruction that would add content the source does not carry.

The Arabic names the narration's real source (Abu Dawud) for the prayer-at-seven hadith, which the master plan's Prayer Journey also builds on. Deleting a correct attribution would make it less verifiable, not safer; the English reproduces the Arabic citation faithfully. Policy question for Khaled: keep or drop explicit non-Sahihayn citations in existing content.
